manual_pass.reason: Accepted: this completed one-life Trial exhausted its full allotted budget, including 8,400 seconds of recorded timeout credits (14 timeouts). It ended at deadline without a native death or verified win. Preserve the original deadline and evidence; this acceptance corrects the scorer's coverage mismatch only and does not claim a win.

interview.hardest_part: Late-game document complexity and time pressure: after day 15-20 the ruleset becomes extremely dense with multiple document types, cross-referencing requirements, encrypted ciphers, and entrant details that must match across 4-6 documents while the clock runs. A single overlooked discrepancy causes citation penalties that reduce daily earnings below survival threshold.
interview.likely_failure: Economic collapse between days 10-20: the game requires processing enough entrants per day to cover rent, heat, food, and medicine while avoiding citation penalties. As document complexity scales and my processing speed remains bounded by turn-based screenshot analysis, daily throughput will drop below the income threshold needed to keep family members alive. Story progression halts when unable to pay rent or after multiple family deaths.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Turn-based advantage: the game pauses while I analyze each screenshot, removing reaction-time pressure and allowing careful document inspection. Clear visual feedback: discrepancies are verifiable through direct comparison of printed details. Deterministic rules: the admission logic is consistent and learnable. Mouse-only input: no complex key combinations or timing required.
interview.harmful_mechanics: Real-time workday clock: each action consumes simulation time even though I choose slowly, limiting daily throughput. Escalating complexity: new document types, rules, and cross-checks are introduced each day without reducing entrant quotas. Economic pressure: fixed costs scale faster than realistic income given turn-based play speed. Penalty accumulation: citation mistakes compound into unrecoverable economic death spirals. Story branching: late-game endings require specific choices across 29 days that may conflict with economic survival.
